survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) and therefore does not define an assessment sampling frame, plausible values, or a student-level analytic dataset. The document describes governance responsibilities and expenditure structure across national, regional, and local levels in the United Kingdom (with devolved administrations), using descriptive tables rather than statistical estimation. As a result, there are no survey weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight schemes (e.g., BRR/jackknife) to apply. For policy interpretation, the key “weighting” concept is institutional coverage (who is responsible for strategy/intelligence/funding/delivery) rather than statistical representativeness.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a governance and institutional mapping note, not an empirical analysis of student achievement or other PV-based cognitive outcomes. Because it does not use ILSA microdata with plausible values, PV handling is not applicable. Similarly, there is no missing-data mechanism to report because no statistical model is estimated on incomplete student responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used descriptive information and OECD compilation sources to map governance responsibilities for the United Kingdom adult skills system; no student-level analytic sample or inclusion/exclusion criteria are defined.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD United Kingdom country note summarizes how the adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels, focusing primarily on England within a combined UK system. It reports the allocation of responsibilities across policy areas (VET, HVET, CET, AE, and ALMP) and governance functions (strategy, intelligence, implementation, funding, delivery) using descriptive tables and an infographic. The note highlights asymmetric decentralisation in England, with Strategic Authorities (including 11 Combined Authorities and the Greater London Authority) allocating funding and managing adult training provision, while Local Authorities and local providers deliver services and support disadvantaged groups. It also describes the roles of national regulators and agencies (e.g., DfE, DWP, Ofsted, Ofqual, OfS) and the planned reform establishing Skills England. No ILSA assessment data, sampling, scaling, or predictive modeling is conducted, so there are no ML performance metrics or achievement benchmarks.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical large-scale assessment study; it is a policy/governance mapping note. Consequently, fields required for ILSA-based empirical ML (student sample sizes, PV handling, missing-data strategy, and model-based findings) are structurally absent by design. The extraction therefore records only the institutional and responsibility structure described in the document, without fabricating any quantitative ML results.
